tested_formulations.mechanism: Abaqus/Standard calculates stabilization damping from continuum element volume and strain energy. Because the entire model consists exclusively of User Elements (UEL U1/U2), continuum element energy is zero, causing internal damping factor evaluation to fail.

tested_formulations.mechanism: Abaqus stabilization damping applies viscous resistance strictly to standard structural degrees of freedom (DOF 1 and 2), not to the user-defined phase-field damage degree of freedom (DOF 3). Consequently, the localized softening snapback at the crack tip (d advancing by +0.052) produces a negative tangent stiffness in the coupled system that standard Newton-Raphson cannot regularize.

standing_policy_decision.rationale: Empirical testing on the cluster demonstrated that Abaqus automatic stabilization either aborts immediately due to UEL incompatibility or fails to traverse the localized crack-tip snapback at t=0.0366. Submitting Package 81 would constitute an unproductive rerun without resolving the numerical blocker, violating Standing Research Execution Rule 4.

recommended_alternatives.description: Step 2 achieves complete mechanical equilibrium under the injected damage field (residual force < 1e-15 kN). Instead of attempting an artificial static coupled relaxation under fixed displacement (which induces an unconstrained snap-through), resume physical displacement loading u_top > 0.002540107 mm directly from the relaxed Step 2 state. Monotonically increasing external work naturally stabilizes crack advancement under standard incrementation.
